function: Over-the-air aggregation of local models in decentralized FL: joint design of MIMO transmit/receive beamformers and the mixing matrix that minimizes a convergence bound (pp. 13-14).
system: Decentralized D2D ad hoc network of M=30 devices, each with NT=NR=20 antennas (10 in benchmark runs), in-band full-duplex, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 7, 19, 23).
method: Decentralized FL (gossip SGD with a mixing matrix) of a CNN on MNIST; beamformers and mixing matrix designed by alternating optimization (convex QCQP), not learned (pp. 6-7, 14-17).
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. Rayleigh fading, global CSI assumed available (pp. 8, 19); MNIST with 20k training and 10k validation samples, heterogeneous split by class (p. 17).
test_conditions: Each setting trained for T=150 rounds, validated on 10k held-out MNIST samples; sweeps over antennas, SNR, devices, sparsity; no unseen channel model or scenario (pp. 17-22).
baselines: Digital 16-bit transmission, zero-forcing beamforming [17], MMSE beamforming with random mixing matrix, joint optimization with separate OTA aggregation (based on [37]), centralized FL [36], error-free case (pp. 19, 22-23).
metrics: Minimum test accuracy among devices, average test accuracy of the global model average, communication NMSE in dB (pp. 18-19).
complexity: Worst-case order O(Jmax(I1max M N^3.5 + I2max M^7)), N = NT, for the alternating optimization algorithm (p. 17).
q1_support: p. 19: "independently and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Rayleigh fading". Not met: custom simulator with textbook fading; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 17: "20k samples to train the model and 10k samples for validation from the original data set". Not met: validation is a held-out part of the same MNIST data, and the sweeps over antennas, SNR, devices, and sparsity (pp. 19-22) are run with their own training (p. 19: "training round T = 150"), with no unseen channel or scenario.
q3_support: p. 23: "transmit and receive beamforming using the zero-forcing criterion [17]" (earlier published over-the-air design, with a random mixing matrix); p. 22: "Digital communication without mixing matrix optimization (DC w/o MMO)" (non-learned digital baseline). Figs. 8-9 (pp. 23-24) compare test accuracy. Borderline: JO with SOA and MB w/o MMO are variants defined by the paper.
q4_support: p. 17: "the worst-case complexity of Algorithm 2 can be expressed as O(Jmax" followed by (I1max M N 3.5 + I2max M 7 ) with N = NT; Algorithm 2 designs the beamformers and the mixing matrix.
q5_support: p. 17: "image classification on the MNIST dataset". Not met: MNIST is a public dataset of the learning task only, the channels are simulated (p. 19), and the paper gives no link to code or data.
notes: Included in area 7: the learned element is the CNN trained across devices with decentralized FL, and the problem solved is the over-the-air aggregation itself (MIMO beamformers plus mixing matrix, pp. 13-14); the physical-layer design is classical alternating optimization, which passes no_learning under the federated-learning-over-the-air rule. System check passes: NT=NR=20 antennas (p. 19). q3 is borderline: the learned-baseline role is played by the zero-forcing design of [17] adapted with a random mixing matrix, while JO with SOA (special case of the design of [37], p. 22) is close to a time-division variant of the proposed scheme (p. 7, footnote 1); the reviewer should confirm. The PDF is arXiv 2310.05075v1 (8 Oct 2023), titled Decentralized Federated Learning via MIMO Over-the-Air Computation: Consensus Analysis and Performance Optimization.
